title: Country Relational Atlas Method
purpose: Promote the reusable country blueprint and coupled-capability logic developed across repository work and prior conversations. This method governs how countries should be represented under WORLD.
fundamental_rule: A country is not an isolated profile. It is a bundle of capabilities, dependencies, institutions, assets, obligations and relationships that only become meaningful in a network.
country_sequence: what it can only do with others
what others can only do with it

cross_cutting_variables.resilience: Capacity to absorb, adapt to and recover from shocks across multiple systems.
cross_cutting_variables.efficiency_vs_resilience: Highly optimized systems may reduce redundancy and cost while increasing fragility; the atlas should make this tradeoff visible.
cross_cutting_variables.defense_industrial_coupling: Defense spending can create domestic R&D, production capacity, procurement networks, jobs and strategic autonomy.
cross_cutting_variables.reciprocal_capability: Countries can become more capable through interaction rather than merely exchanging goods.
cross_cutting_variables.partial_functional_integration: Deep cooperation can exist without full political or institutional merger.
cross_cutting_variables.coupled_capability: A capability available only because multiple countries contribute complementary assets or permissions.

data_rule: Replace placeholders with real sourced information. When data is unknown, mark it unknown rather than fabricating completion.
blueprint_growth_rule: If a useful field repeatedly appears across countries, add it to the blueprint so the method becomes richer over time.
